dialogues.speaker: Linling
dialogues.text: I'm Linling. I'm the registrar for all the boats in these docks...

dialogues.speaker: Linling
dialogues.text: ...Actually, I'm employed by the Commerce Guild to do menial tasks for all those stuffy old business people...

dialogues.speaker: Linling
dialogues.text: But never mind all that. When you're young, you should fix your vision on something with broad horizons, right?

dialogues.speaker: Linling
dialogues.text: Just look how beautiful the sea is today, it's so tranquil! As I like to say, "To be blind to the beauty that poets adore is to view the world from the ocean floor."

dialogues.speaker: Linling
dialogues.text: Hehehe, I composed that poem myself. Isn't it philosophical?

response.speaker: Linling
response.text: What did you say!? Let me tell you something, I have a poetic gift and I'm gonna be a household name one day! Just like the great poet Qingzhou!

response.speaker: Linling
response.text: Hmph. Commoners don't like my poetry, those lords of the Qixing Commerce Guild don't appreciate my hard work, and this dull job is so far below my aspirations...

response.speaker: Linling
response.text: Is it any wonder that I'm out here staring aimlessly at the sea...

choices.text: Do you have Anemo power? Because girl, your poetry just blew me away.

response.speaker: Linling
response.text: Why thank you! You have wonderful taste in poetry. Only a small number of rare geniuses see true reason, and it seems you are one of them — just like me!

response.speaker: Linling
response.text: The way I see it, the Qixing aren't all that. Who knows, I might do a better job than them.

response.speaker: Linling
response.text: I mean, let's be honest. They just follow the divine predictions we receive from Rex Lapis during the Rite of Descension to the letter. It's all his work, so what are they so uppity about?

response.speaker: Linling
response.text: ...Uh, did I just say that a bit too loud?
